subject: Literature
title: Arthur Koestler's Darkness at Noon
description: A quick, practical guide to Arthur Koestler's Darkness at Noon.

hook.text: Darkness at Noon is about a loyal revolutionary who is arrested, tortured, and forced to confess to crimes he never committed.

buildup.text: Rubashov, the protagonist, was modeled on real Bolsheviks who confessed to fabricated charges during Stalin's show trials.

discovery.text: The novel reveals how totalitarian logic traps believers: if the Party is always right, then dissent is always treason.

twist.text: Koestler himself was a former communist who had narrowly escaped execution during the Spanish Civil War.

climax.text: The book became the most powerful literary indictment of Stalinism and helped shift Western intellectual opinion.

punchline.text: A former true believer wrote the best argument against belief.

quiz.question: What real historical events inspired Darkness at Noon?
options: The Nazi concentration camps during World War II
Stalin's show trials where loyal Bolsheviks confessed to fabricated charges
